requirement.evidence: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause” (previously called “good cause”).
requirement.note: The nonpayment threshold of one month's FMR in the Oakland-Fremont HUD Metro FMR is also stated in the document.

key_value.evidence: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR

effective_date.note: Field is empty on the card.

status.evidence: Eviction for nonpayment of rent is no longer permitted for rental debt of less than one month’s Fair Market Rent for a unit of equivalent size.
status.note: The document presents the rule as current law.

coverage.note: Field is empty on the card.

citation.note: Measure BB and the November 2024 election are supported. The document does not give the ordinance's full name, 'Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance', and states no code section.

requirement.evidence: This cap does not prevent a landlord who has “banked” (unused) AGAs from previous years from implementing a rent increase that is greater than 5% in order to raise the rent to the rent ceiling.
requirement.note: The document also says the maximum AGA is 5% and that the AGA is the amount by which a landlord of a fully covered unit may raise the rent each year.

key_value.evidence: The elected Rent Board sets the AGA by following a formula in the Rent Ordinance that ties the AGA to the Consumer Price Index.
key_value.note: The 5% maximum is also stated: 'The maximum AGA is 5%.'
